items.title: Ship traffic halts in Strait of Hormuz as U.S. blockade begins

featured_image.name: What a US-led Hormuz strait naval blockade would look like ...

items.description:
Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz appeared to halt on Monday after President Donald Trump announced on social media that the United States would blockade the critical waterway, sending oil prices surging and deepening a global energy crisis triggered by weeks of conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran.

Lloyd's List Intelligence reported that ships had stopped moving through the strait, while Brent crude surged more than 8 percent to above $103 per barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude jumped roughly 8 percent past $104. Wholesale gasoline prices spiked 6 percent and heating oil climbed 10 percent in early trading.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Pope Leo says he does not fear Trump amid Iran war feud

featured_image.name: Trump Berates Pope Leo

items.description:
Pope Leo XIV on Monday said he has "no intention to debate" with President Donald Trump, hours after the U.S. president launched a sweeping attack on the pontiff over his condemnation of the war in Iran. Speaking to reporters aboard a papal flight to Algiers, where he is beginning a 10-day tour of Africa, the pope said he would not be deterred from advocating for peace.[1][2]

"I will continue to speak out loudly against war, looking to promote peace, promoting dialogue and multilateral relationships among the states to look for just solutions to problems," Leo told Reuters. "Too many people are suffering in the world today. Too many innocent people are being killed. And I think someone has to stand up and say, 'There's a better way.'"[2]

items.title: China dismisses Iran arms reports as 'baseless smears' amid Trump tariff threat

featured_image.name: Chinese FM addresses inquiry regarding Iranian ambassador ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump warned on Sunday that China would face a 50 per cent tariff on all goods entering the United States if Beijing is found to be supplying weapons to Iran, escalating a confrontation that now spans the Middle East conflict, nuclear diplomacy and global trade.

The threat came hours after marathon US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad collapsed without agreement, and as a CNN report citing three US intelligence sources indicated that China is preparing to deliver shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missile systems, known as MANPADs, to Tehran within weeks.[1][2]

items.title: Eni CEO urges EU to rethink Russian gas ban ahead of April 25 deadline

featured_image.name: Descalzi gets third term as Eni chief executive officer ...

items.description:
Claudio Descalzi, chief executive of Italian energy group Eni, called on the European Union to rethink its plan to progressively ban imports of Russian gas from the start of 2027, warning that the bloc has no clear way to replace the supplies it stands to lose.

Speaking on Sunday at an event organized by Italy's co-ruling League party, Descalzi said it was unclear how Europe could substitute roughly 20 billion cubic meters of Russian gas, which he described as providing vital flexibility to the continent's power stations, according to Reuters. He called the ongoing conflict in Iran "the most significant event of the last 40 years" in terms of energy supply disruption.[1][2][3]

items.title: European stocks slide as US-Iran talks collapse, oil tops $100

featured_image.name: Trump announces naval blockade on Iran after peace talks ...

items.description:
European stocks opened sharply lower on Monday as investors reacted to the breakdown of marathon peace negotiations between the United States and Iran, while a fresh threat to blockade the Strait of Hormuz sent oil prices surging back above $100 a barrel.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 slipped 0.8% in early trading, with losses steeper across major national indices. Germany's DAX fell as much as 1.45%, France's CAC 40 declined 1%, and the FTSE 100 dropped around 0.6%, according to CNBC and IG data. US stock futures also pointed lower.[1][2][3]

items.title: China's Q1 GDP expected to rebound to 4.8% amid Iran war risks

featured_image.name: China's economy capable of staging relatively fast growth in ...

items.description:
China's economy is expected to have regained momentum in the first quarter of 2026, but economists warn that the ongoing war in Iran threatens to drag on growth for the rest of the year as energy costs rise and global demand weakens.

Gross domestic product likely grew 4.8% year-on-year in the January-March period, up from a 4.5% pace in the fourth quarter of 2025, according to a Reuters poll of 50 economists published on Monday. The rebound was driven by robust exports, particularly in electronics and AI-related products, and recovering investment. Beijing is scheduled to release the official Q1 GDP figures alongside March activity data on Thursday, April 16.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Wise reports 26% Q4 volume surge ahead of May Nasdaq debut

featured_image.name: Kristo Käärmann | Co-founder and CEO, Wise

items.description:
British fintech group Wise reported on Monday that cross-border transaction volumes rose 26 percent in the fourth quarter to £49.4 billion ($66.2 billion), reinforcing expectations that its full-year profit margin will land at the top end of its forecast range as the company prepares for its Nasdaq debut.[1][2]

The London-listed money transfer firm said it expects to complete its planned dual listing and begin trading on the Nasdaq from May 11, marking a milestone in its shift toward the US capital markets. As part of the transition, Wise will report its fiscal 2026 results in US dollars under US GAAP accounting standards.[2][1]

items.title: South Korea, Poland upgrade ties in first shift in 13 years

featured_image.name: South Korea and Poland to upgrade ties as Tusk calls Seoul key ally ...

items.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae-myung and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk agreed on Monday to elevate bilateral relations to a "comprehensive strategic partnership," marking the first upgrade in ties since the two countries established a strategic partnership in 2013.[1][2][3]

The announcement came during a summit at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, during what was the first bilateral visit by a Polish prime minister to South Korea in 27 years and Tusk's first bilateral visit to a non-European country since taking office.[4][5][1]

items.title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Algeria on historic first papal visit

featured_image.name: In Algeria, Saint Augustine's city anticipates Pope Leo's visit

items.description: Pope Leo XIV departed Rome on Monday for Algeria, becoming the first pope ever to visit the North African nation and launching an ambitious 11-day tour of four African countries aimed at strengthening Christian-Muslim dialogue and honoring the legacy of St. Augustine.[1][2][3]

items.title: Starmer and Macron call for de-escalation and Lebanon ceasefire

featured_image.name: U.K., French and German leaders press Israel over Gaza aid ...

items.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke on Sunday, April 12, issuing a joint call for de-escalation in the Middle East and insisting that any ceasefire must extend to Lebanon, according to an official readout from Downing Street. The conversation came hours after US President Donald Trump announced the US Navy would blockade the Strait of Hormuz following the collapse of marathon peace talks between the US and Iran in Islamabad.[1]

items.title: Trump calls Pope Leo XIV 'weak' as Vatican feud escalates over Iran war

featured_image.name: Trump Criticizes Pope Leo, Accuses Him of Catering to ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump launched a broadside against Pope Leo XIV on Sunday, calling the pontiff "WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy" in a social media post that marked the sharpest public clash yet between the White House and the Vatican over the U.S.-led war in Iran.[1][2][3]

Writing on Truth Social, Trump urged the first American-born pope to "stop appeasing the Radical Left," escalating a weeks-long feud that has pitted the world's two most prominent Americans against each other on opposite sides of the conflict.[4][1]

items.title: Iran's internet blackout hits 44 days as US talks collapse

featured_image.name: Iran's 44-day internet blackout breaks global records as peace talks ...

items.description: Iran's nationwide internet blackout has entered its 44th consecutive day, surpassing 1,032 hours and setting what monitors describe as the longest nation-scale internet shutdown ever recorded in any country. The milestone comes as high-stakes peace talks between Washington and Tehran collapsed in Islamabad on Sunday without agreement, casting doubt over a fragile ceasefire set to expire on 22 April.

items.title: Starmer and Macron agree on Hormuz coalition in call after Iran talks collapse

featured_image.name: Macron, Starmer pledge deeper ties between France and ...

items.description:
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and French President Emmanuel Macron spoke by phone on Sunday, agreeing on the need for de-escalation across the Middle East and pledging joint efforts to protect freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an official readout from Downing Street .

The leaders stressed the importance of a lasting ceasefire that includes Lebanon to support wider regional stability, and agreed on the "strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz for global trade and energy supplies," the readout said, adding that both would work "with a wide coalition of partners to protect freedom of navigation" .

items.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for ceasefire in Ukraine, Lebanon, Sudan

featured_image.name: Cease fire' Pope Leo asks world leaders as he expresses ...

items.description:
Pope Leo XIV issued urgent appeals for peace in Ukraine, Lebanon, and Sudan on Sunday, using his Regina Caeli address on Divine Mercy Sunday to call on warring parties to lay down their arms and protect civilians caught in conflict.

Speaking to pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square on April 12, the pope invoked international humanitarian principles as he demanded immediate action. "The principle of humanity, inscribed in the conscience of every person and recognized in international law, entails the moral obligation to protect the civilian population from the horrific effects of war," he said. "I call on the parties in the conflict to declare a ceasefire and urgently seek a peaceful solution."[1][2]

items.title: Israeli strike kills toddler at her father's funeral in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israeli strikes kill at least 18 people across southern Lebanon

items.description:
Israeli military strikes killed at least 97 people and wounded 133 others across southern Lebanon in a single 24-hour period ending Saturday, pushing the cumulative death toll past 2,000 since the war between Israel and Hezbollah erupted on March 2, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry.[1][2]

The ministry said in a statement Saturday evening that at least 2,020 people have now been killed and 6,436 wounded, including 165 children and 248 women. Nearly one million people have been displaced from their homes across the country.[2][3][4]

items.title: McIlroy wins back-to-back Masters titles at Augusta

featured_image.name: Rory McIlroy wins Masters 2026 to become fourth man to ...

items.description: Rory McIlroy claimed his second consecutive green jacket on Sunday at Augusta National, finishing at 12 under par to become the fourth player in Masters history to win the tournament in back-to-back years, joining Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo, and Tiger Woods.[1][2][3]

items.title: CENTCOM to begin blockade of Iranian ports Monday

featured_image.name: US Central Command announces blockade of all Iranian ports ...

items.description: U.S. Central Command announced Sunday that American naval forces will begin enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports on Monday, April 13, at 10 a.m. ET, following President Donald Trump's order after U.S.-Iran nuclear negotiations ended without an agreement. The blockade marks a dramatic escalation in the conflict that has upended global energy markets since late February.[1][2]

items.title: An Iraqi drone narrowly missed a convoy carrying a freed US journalist in Baghdad

featured_image.name: Iraq's militia state: Shelly Kittleson's kidnapping exposes who runs ...

items.description: A drone attack by an unidentified Iran-backed Iraqi militia narrowly missed a U.S. diplomatic convoy transporting freed American journalist Shelly Kittleson through Baghdad International Airport on April 8, according to a senior Iraqi security official who spoke to Agence France-Presse. The incident, which came just one day after Kittleson's release from a week of captivity, underscored the persistent dangers facing American personnel in Iraq amid escalating regional hostilities.[1][2]

items.title: U.S.-Iran talks end without deal as UN chief calls Hormuz tolls unlawful

featured_image.name: In conversation with IMO Sec-Gen Arsenio Dominguez ahead of ...

items.description: The head of the International Maritime Organization declared that Iran's effort to levy tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz is unlawful and must be resisted by the international community, as shipping through the critical waterway remains a fraction of pre-war levels despite a fragile ceasefire now days old.

items.title: UK refuses to join Trump's Strait of Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: UK, France eye warships, mine-hunting drones to break Iran's grip ...

items.description:
The United Kingdom confirmed on Sunday that it will not join President Donald Trump's newly announced naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, directly contradicting Trump's own claims that Britain was among the countries assisting with the operation.

Trump announced the blockade in a post on Truth Social hours after US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad collapsed without a deal. "Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," he wrote. In a later interview with Fox News, Trump said, "The U.K. and a couple of other countries are sending mine sweepers".[1][2]

That claim was swiftly rebuffed by London. A UK government spokesperson told CBS News that Britain would not be involved in the blockade and was instead "urgently working with France and other partners to put together a wide coalition to protect freedom of navigation". The spokesperson added: "The Strait of Hormuz must not be subject to tolling".[3][2]
